text:
sara: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a per-route trace retention model (not just env-level). Thinking: some high-cardinality ingestion routes (uploads, parsing) should be cold by default, while API gateway traces stay hot for longer. Want feedback on console exposure vs infra-only config. :thinking:

vikram: +1 to per-route. We get a lot of noise from worker jobs that inflate storage. Do you mean user-exposed controls (slider) or YAML only?

sara: Ideally both. Admins could set defaults in infra YAML, product teams could tune per-route via Console for routes they own. But worried about support surface and accidental long-retains.

elaine: Major consideration: query performance. Our hot index layout assumes recent TTLs. If routes diverge a lot we may need more index shard splitting or per-route index tags which complicates the exporter.

ben: Also think about multi-tenant safety — a single tenant route with 1yr retention could blow cost. Need hard caps by tenant/account level.

tony: What about having a policy layer: route -> retention window + rehydrate policy + query-priority? Then Console only shows "effective retention" and a toggle to request increase (requires approval). Keeps config centralized.

vikram: That sounds good. Operationally, rehydrate jobs are expensive. If we give per-route long-retains, we need cheap on-demand rehydrate and a UI for estimated cost/time. Otherwise SRE will get paged.

infra-bot: deploy:telemetry-config v0.23 deployed to staging — exporter config schema changed: added `route_retention` block.

sara: Example schema I'm testing (staging):
```yaml
telemetry:
  exporters:
    otlp:
      endpoint: otlp.internal:4317
  route_retention:
    default_days: 30
    overrides:
      - route: "api.upload.v1"
        retention_days: 90
      - route: "worker.cleanup"
        retention_days: 7
    tenant_hard_cap_days: 180
    rehydrate_window_days: 7
```

elaine: Nice. Couple of notes: 1) rehydrate_window_days should be per-category (fast vs bulk). 2) We need a background compaction to prune index keys for routes that go cold to reduce disk and query fanout.

ben: For telemetry pipeline: exporter needs to tag spans with route and tenant at ingestion. If route tag missing fallback to service.name, but that hurts correctness. We should add a span-processor that normalizes route tag.

vikram: How do we handle backwards compatibility for existing traces? If someone changes default from 30->7, do we expire older ones immediately? Need clear semantics: config is about future ingestion, and we provide a migration/retention job to mutate existing TTLs only via explicit admin action.

sara: Agreed. Change semantics: defaults are for new spans; explicit admin action triggers a backfill/trim job with audit log. Console shows a changelog and an "apply to past data" button with cost estimate.

tony: UX request: in Console don't expose exact days in some modes — show buckets (1w, 1m, 3m, 6m, custom) and highlight cost delta per bucket (tokens/GB/day). Less config noise.

elaine: We'll need telemetry metrics for: per-route storage bytes, rehydrate ops/sec, percent of queries hitting cold tier, and query latency P50/P95 by tier. Add dashboards early.

sara: One subtle thing — exporters currently batch by service.name. If route retention diverges, batching should be by retention class to avoid mixing hot and cold writes. That may reduce batch efficiency. Tradeoff.

ben: Could we do hybrid: write all spans to hot for X days, then snapshot to cold longer-term store (object storage) with trace chunk index referencing object keys. Queries older than X hit object store + partial rehydrate. That keeps recent queries fast and caps hot index size.

vikram: That's basically hot-window snapshotting. Works but we need a rehydration cache for frequently queried cold traces to avoid repeated expensive calls. Also enforce tenant_hard_cap during snapshot stage.

tony: On API surface debate: exposing retention per-route in internal API (and Console) opens automation (CD pipelines can set policy). If we keep it infra-only, product teams must file infra tickets. Which do we prefer?

sara: Prefer API + RBAC: only route owners and infra-admins can set policy. Auditor role sees change history. Otherwise this will bottleneck.

elaine: From infra perspective we need a safe rollout path: feature-flag console exposure, shadow reads, and sampling rollout. Also test queries against mixed-retention test-set.

ben: Security: ensure KMS policies and cold-store encryption metadata maintained across snapshot/rehydrate. Also ensure deleted traces are removed from both hot and cold stores per retention.

vikram: Operational playbook items: automated alert if hot-index grows > 1.5x forecast for 7 days, and "unexpected cold reads" rate spike which may indicate bad retention setting.

sara: I'll open an RFC with the schema, Console mockups, and a small POC that implements route tagging + snapshotting. Plan: 2-week spike, then canary to a single team.

tony: Sounds good. Please add an acceptance checklist including: tenant hard caps, admin audit, rehydrate cost estimate, exporter tagging, and dashboards.

sara: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: note: RFC draft created — /rfc/telemetry/per-route-retention-1994556789 -> reviewers: @vikram @elaine @ben

vikram: Reviewing today. Quick Q: do we want a separate quota metric for trace storage per-account to surface in Billing? That would help product send alerts before hitting cap.

ben: Yes — expose "trace_storage_bytes" and computed "projected_days_remaining". Billing team can pipe alerts.

elaine: I'll add dashboard panels for that.

sara: Closing loop: post-RFC spike we'll demo Console flow and cost estimates. If folks have objections to per-route exposure vs infra-only call them out on the RFC thread.

vikram: Thanks — this is a better direction than one-size-fits-all. :thumbsup:
